# Welcome and opening keynotes

Day 1, 11:00 · Lino Cattaruzzi, President, Google Iberia · coverage: slides, transcript

Covers two agenda slots: the 11:00 Welcome (event host) and the 11:20 Opening keynote by Lino Cattaruzzi, named in the host's on-stage hand-over; he also presented the Larry Page quote and the five ecosystem principles. Transcript from a second attendee recording; an audio recording covers the keynote from its first minute to the end.

## Claims

- **[Slide]** The keynote showed a slide quoting Elizabeth Reid (VP, Search) saying Search is never a solved problem because the internet and the world keep changing.
  > "Search is never a solved problem. Old challenges evolve and new challenges are constantly popping up — because the internet and the world are always changing."
  <br><sub>`D1-C001` · Day 1, Welcome and opening keynotes (Lino Cattaruzzi, President, Google Iberia) · Extended by [D1-C182](D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google named three forces driving the evolution of Search: new platforms (closed-garden apps taking information needs from the open web), new user preferences (personalised, authentic, visual, easy-to-parse content) and new technologies (AI and ML).
  <br><sub>`D1-C002` · Day 1, Welcome and opening keynotes (Lino Cattaruzzi, President, Google Iberia)</sub>

- **[Slide]** The stated theme guiding the future of Search is making it effortless to find helpful information.
  > "Making it effortless to find helpful information"
  <br><sub>`D1-C003` · Day 1, Welcome and opening keynotes (Lino Cattaruzzi, President, Google Iberia)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google says users like AI Overviews and search more because of them, with early feedback overwhelmingly positive and satisfaction highest among 18–24 year olds.
  <br><sub>`D1-C004` · Day 1, Welcome and opening keynotes (Lino Cattaruzzi, President, Google Iberia) · not in Google docs · Extended by [D1-C184](D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md) · Extended by [D3-C569](D3-S16-mastering-the-messy-middle.md)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google says AI Overviews help with new types of questions and lead users to visit a greater diversity of sites, with more total sites shown on the results page.

- **[Slide]** Google reports more than 5 trillion searches per year.
  <br><sub>`D1-C006` · Day 1, Welcome and opening keynotes (Lino Cattaruzzi, President, Google Iberia) · confirmed by Google docs · [AI, personalization and the future of shopping](https://blog.google/products/ads-commerce/ai-personalization-and-the-future-of-shopping/) · Repeated by [D2-C752](D2-S24-google-trends.md)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's opening slide described AI as driving an expansionary moment for Search.
  <br><sub>`D1-C135` · Day 1, Welcome and opening keynotes (Lino Cattaruzzi, President, Google Iberia)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google says 94% of frequent LLM users are also frequent users of Google Search, as evidence that AI is growing search use rather than replacing it.

- **[Slide]** Google says 71% of shoppers coming to Google Search agree they are open to trying new brands or products (the slide footnote cites a Google-commissioned Ipsos global consumer survey), and that people use Search to figure out what they want, not only to find what they already know.
  <br><sub>`D1-C008` · Day 1, Welcome and opening keynotes (Lino Cattaruzzi, President, Google Iberia) · not in Google docs</sub>

  <br><sub>`D1-C009` · Day 1, Welcome and opening keynotes (Lino Cattaruzzi, President, Google Iberia)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Ecosystem principle 1, consistent testing: features are tested and woven into core Search when ready.
  <br><sub>`D1-C010` · Day 1, Welcome and opening keynotes (Lino Cattaruzzi, President, Google Iberia)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Ecosystem principle 2, the SERP will evolve: besides organic links and ads, it will hold other elements such as videos and cards.

- **[Slide]** Ecosystem principle 3, multiple user needs: some users want links, some quick answers, some depth; Google says it will keep prioritising traffic to the ecosystem.
  <br><sub>`D1-C012` · Day 1, Welcome and opening keynotes (Lino Cattaruzzi, President, Google Iberia)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Ecosystem principle 4, incentivise high-quality content: content made for Search will not be successful.
  > "Made for Search" content will not be successful, as we'll work to incentivise high-quality content."

- **[Analysis]** Principle 5 is the one to plan around. Growth is in brainstorming, 'which' and planning queries, which are comparison-style needs that a page answering a single keyword fits poorly.
